title: Bull call spread after a sell-off: ON Semiconductor 100/110
summary: For a beaten-down stock you still like, the speaker buys a bull call spread to add convexity. The ON Semiconductor 100/110 call spread costs about $3.50 for a $10 width and expires in six months. If the stock rises roughly 25%, it makes about 186%. Breakeven is $103.50 and the probability of profit is about 29%. Take it only if you think the odds are higher.

steps.caption: ON trades near $88 after a sharp drop. The spread sits above the market.
Buy the $100 call and sell the $110 call, six months out.
The payoff: risk about $3.50 for a $10 wide spread.
Below $100 at expiry you lose the full $3.50 debit.
Breakeven is $103.50. The market gives about a 29% chance of finishing above it.
Above $110, a rise of about 25%, the spread makes $6.50: about 186% on the debit.
Before expiry the value moves slowly. Most of the gain comes late if the stock recovers.

takeaways: A bull call spread adds defined-risk upside to a stock that has fallen.
ON 100/110 for about $3.50: about 186% profit potential with a $103.50 breakeven.
The market implies about a 29% probability of profit.
Take the trade only if you believe the real probability is higher than 29%.
caveats: The speaker says this is education, not a recommendation; prices are from the clip date and the stock price here is estimated.
His 2.9:1 figure compares the $10 width with the debit; reward to risk on the $6.50 net gain is about 1.9:1, below the owner's 2:1 X09 rule.

backtest.note: Six-month out-of-the-money bull call spread on beaten-down chip names; take profit near 150% of the debit.
